title: Grim Reach Idle 1.3 - Sharing My Journey and Experiences releasing and maintaining a semi-successfull AI Steam Game
author: Shalke97
selftext:
Hello Reddit, it's me again and no you probably won't remember. A few months ago i made a post here About my heavily AI assisted Idle Game, "Grim Reach Idle".



Before i start, i just want to say that i deeply respect this Sub, so i won't be using any AI assistence for this post, please keep that in mind when reading because english is not my native language.

A few days ago i launched a Major updated and i thought it is time for another post to tell everyone About it, while also spreading some Knowledge About Things i learned on this journey. Quick info regarding my game. It's an OSRS inspired Dark Fantasy Idle RPG, in a gritty World with its own universe around it. You have gather skills, crafting skills, skills that send you out to fight and skills like farming and hunting which are rather passive. I don't really want to go into much detail about the game itself, if you're interested about it, check out the steam page yourself and give it a look!

# Experiences and Tips.

Before i go into more detail about the update, i want to share my experiences with you because that is probably what most of you are interested in. First we'll talk numbers.

I launched the game into EA, because i wasn't really sure how i'd imagine the finished 1.0 version. The shop site was only up for two weeks before i was able to publish my game, i didn't have patience, i didn't do marketing and i wasn't really working on wishlist additions. I just wanted to get my game out there and so i did. I even released it a day before the announced release date, because of a mistake of mine. This mistake cost me some positive reviews, since i didn't upload the polished build but a version before that, so there were two major bugs that people really hindered. 80% of my to date bad reviews come from this launch issue. Surprisingly there was no backlash at all regarding the use of AI anything. My store page claims that the Art Assets are AI generated because of my budget and that is true. I didn't state that the code is also 99,9% AI based, why? Because you are not obligated to, simple as that. There are people out there, that will hate AI without reason and it doesn't matter in the finished game, if i wrote the code myself or if the code was AI generated. I'm a software developer IRL and i didn't type a single line of code in months. Back to EA, the launch was surprisingly good, the first day sold around 90 Units, which was a really great experience, people actually cared and played the game. So of course, i was deeply motivated to keep going and so i did.

While working on the 1.0 Version of the game, i kept interacting with people on my community hub and worked on their feedback. The first thing i added for 1.0 was a bug report system and you should do to. It's an easy setup with a discord channel you create, webhooks and integration inside your game. If someone reports something ingame, it will send the attached image and text to my discord server and this helped massively. Reports came in, i basically threw them at claude and he worked on a fix. So i could focus on going forward, while claude was going backwards fixing what was broken and overlooked. After a month i was already feeling that i was close to my imagined 1.0 Version so i decided to release it out of early access after one month, which i know, is very controversal. But it worked out!

And here is the first really important Info most you might not now. Your Launch is your biggest selling opportunity. I knew that before but i underestimated the real effect here. My store page views sky rocketed and i sold around 90 Units a day for a week. Which in hindsight could've been much more, if i had focussed more on marketing and wishlists. After the initial launch week, things simmered down to around 10 Sales per day. And thats where i am sitting right now, since then, my daily sales tend to be around 5-10 Units. You might think that is enough but keep in mind, the dashboard numbers on your steam game are still calculated without the 30% share you have to give to steam.

# So, what are the numbers, after exactly 3 Months? Thats what the image is:

You can see that the game is semi-successfull, i'm really proud of the numbers actually. I have around 120 daily players that play and enjoy the game, that feeling alone

was worth everything. Of course, there are also alot of returned units, which isn't uncommon since how easy it is to refund a game on steam these days. But what really struck out are the hardcore fans. Players with 600..800 and even one with 1100 Hours of Playtime, of course its an idler, but to think someone was willing to run my game for that amount of time makes me proud. So thats the way and state of my last 3 months with this game.

***Condensed tips:***

***- Build a Bug Report ingame with Discord Webhooks and a new Discord Channel.***

***- Interact with your community, don't ignore criticism but face it with pride and reason.***

***- Don't get demotivated by low numbers, we all started this because we wanted to make a game, not to print money.***

***- Build publicly, i didn't and i regret it. I wished i had.***

***- As the Human in your operation, take the reigns of the game design, don't let AI define too much of your game, AI should help you make your ideas.***

***- Ask for help, i've seen alot of posts here the last months, alot of comments of people who start and are oblivious on how things work and what is required. i would never advise someone with a free or 20$ sub to start making a game. The beginning is fast and cheap but the more complex it gets, the more tokens you'll need. (I burned 60 Billion, BILLION, tokens on my  City Builder project last week).***

***- Multi-Language support is a MUST HAVE! My sales are all across the world and i'm certain that was the key to the success i've seen so far. My game is available in Chinese, French, Russian, German, Brazilian Portuguese, Spanish and English. Don't sleep on this, 30% of my sales are from Asia, 20% from Russia. Build your game from scratch with localisation Strings in mind.***

I am, of course, open for any questions regarding my workflow or on how i use AI in general.

# Now, time for my 1.3 Update for Grim Reach Idle!

**1.3 Was supposed to be meaningfull and help the replayability of the game.**

**- New Feature: Ashfall - a prestige system that allows you to start over after meeting certain requirements. This will give you "Scar Points" depending on what you've achieved in this run. After the Ashfall, you'll be able to spend those points on a talent tree that will boost your Save permanently, like minor increased XP rates for certail level ranges, for example. You'll keep important aspects though. Like earned Pets, Achievements, Mastery, Hunting Ledger, Hunter's Codex and the Beastiary.**

**- New Content: The Idol Halls - a new area opened with new enemies, champions aswell as 5 new chapters to the story.**

**- New Content: Slayer Tower expansion - The Slayer tower was expanded upwards, adding 3 new floors to the slayer tower for more dangerously monsters to hunt.**

**- New Content: Paragon Tower expansion - The Paragon tower was expanded aswell, more chest rewards await up until Paragon Level 100.**

**- New Content: Hunter's Codex (85) - to make slayer more relevant in the long run, you'll now have a skill tree built around slayer and slayer points. This skill tree has skills like "Pet Tracking" which will allow you to boost your pet drop chances, to make hunting them a little less painfull. Or Talents which will increased the rare drop chance of slayer monsters and many more. Slayer is now a fundamental skill to progress your Account in the long run. The Hunter's Codex will also sustain after Ashfalling and will be available again to your account after hitting 85 slayer. I know that this is a pretty high requirement, but the talents in the codex are pretty strong for your account. It shouldn't feel like you can cheat your early game with those talents but make the endgame more enjoyable.**

**- New Weapons: Range & Magic Weapon expansion - Before this update, meele had around 18 weapons more than the other two fighting styles. To even things out, 18 new weapons were added across the range and magic skill to give more variety and options in mid to endgame.**

**- New Content: Woodcutting & Fishing expansion - both of those skills simmered down at level 90, now you'll have 3 new trees for the range of 90-99, allowing you to craft new more sophisticated fishing rods. Fishing was alos expanded with 4 new fish and fitting cooking recipes for them.**

**- Ingame Wiki: Everything you find in game, is now included inside a Wiki inside the game itself. You can search up any item or weapon and see where it comes from. So players who like to plan their journey, now finally can.**

**- Companion Overhaul: All earnable ingame pets have been reworked to be more unique and fitting. There is also now an "Echo" system in place, where the passive effect of that pet is always active for 25% of its strength.**

\- Of course this is not all, alot of bug fixes, a new UI look, new Bank and Inventory functions and much more. Thank you for reading and again, i'm always open for any kind of feedback or questions.

\-Adhavar
